Initial evaluation revealed pancytopenia (hemoglobin 9.4 g/dL, leukocytes 1940 cells/µL, neutrophils 230 cells/µL, platelets 61,000 cells/µL) with febrile neutropenia. ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: While bone marrow findings were consistent with AML (42% myeloblasts, CD34+, CD117+, CD13+), the clinical course and final diagnosis of necrotizing fasciitis from carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella indicates the pancytopenia and bone marrow findings were likely secondary to severe infection/sepsis rather than primary hematologic malignancy. The rapid clinical deterioration with perineal infection and multiorgan dysfunction, followed by recovery with surgical debridement and antibiotics, supports infection as the primary process.
